To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) de novo TP53 mutations occur in 14% of LFS patients and (2) approximately one-fifth occur during embryonic life.
(i) 40/328 (12%) TP53 mutation carriers have a de novo mutation and (ii) 6/108 (6%) TP53 mutation-negative patients with LFS spectrum tumours harbour a mosaic TP53 mutation.
de novo mutations are the most frequent mechanism for germline TP553 mutation occurrence in LFS and that mosaic germline TP533 mutation carriers can develop LFS tumours.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and characterisation of the molecular basis of cancer predisposition syndromes, and the clinical and biological consequences of germline TP 53 mutations in Li-Fraumenie Syndrome.
the development and the use of new methods of analysis to identify mutations in the TP53 gene.
the study of TP53 mutations in patients who are suspected of Li-Fraumenisyndrome.

the contribution of de-novo and mosaic TP53 mutation to Li-Fraumani syndrome is 20-25% and the remaining 75% are inherited mutations.

the contribution of de-novo mutations to LFS is 14%, and the contribution of mosaicism is approximately 1.4%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the contribution of de-novo mutations to the Li-Faumeni spectrum is higher than expected, at least 14%, and that the contribution of mosaic mutations should not be neglected.

the identification of a germlin TP53 mutation in a patient should be followed by a careful analysis of the family history, and a search for de novo and mosaic germline TP533 mutations.
